page: Microsoft Azure DC2ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities feature 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA extensions for cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator but includes 81 GB of local SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal solid single-threaded performance contrasted with limited aggregate throughput due to the low core count. The instance achieves a strong stress-ng single-core score of 3015.55 (top 25%) and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1898.0, reflecting modern per-core architecture. In contrast, multi-core metrics settle in the lower tier, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 2333.0 and PassMark CPU scoring 3737.03. Database operations in PassMark (916.95) and Redis SET operations (2.67 million ops/sec) reflect the constraints of a single physical core under concurrent memory and processing contention.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, DC2ads_v6 serves as a balanced entry-level instance with bundled local solid-state storage, eliminating the immediate requirement for attached network disks for temporary data caching. However, the limited core and memory footprint restricts heavy multi-threaded scalability. It is appropriate for lightweight enterprise workloads, edge microservices, small API gateways, CI/CD runners, and development or testing environments.
description: Microsoft Azure DC2ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 2 dedicated vCPUs running across 1 physical core with multithreading, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory and 81 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Compute capabilities feature AVX-512, VAES, and SHA cryptographic extensions alongside a 32 MB L3 cache. Performance metrics demonstrate competitive single-core execution, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 3015.55 and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1898.0. However, multi-core scalability remains modest due to the physical core constraint, as shown by lower PassMark and multi-threaded benchmark scores. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, this instance is best matched with lightweight web services, small microservices, and development environments requiring predictable single-thread performance.
